body:
OBSERVED TWICE ON 2026-07-28, by two independent build lanes running the full suite in sibling
worktrees (T122's and T123's). Both saw test/gateway/write-renderers.test.ts fail under load and pass
clean on isolated rerun. Neither diff touches the file.

MEASURED THE SAME NIGHT, on main: 3 isolated runs pass (7/7 tests, ~2s); 4 CONCURRENT copies of the
file alone all pass. So the reproduction needs heavier contention than the file self-inflicts —
plausibly the full suite in two-plus worktrees, where worker-thread spawn or render timeouts starve.
The failure text was not captured by either lane; capturing it is step one.

THE STANDING RULE (Myk, 2026-07-23) says a flake is fixed NOW; tonight's budget bent that to
diagnose-and-ticket, and this body says so plainly rather than hiding it. The exposure is confined to
concurrent local lanes — single-tree CI has not failed on it — but the rule's point stands: a lane
that learns to rerun a red bar is learning the wrong lesson, so this outranks ordinary queue work the
next time a lane hits it WITH the failure text in hand.

THE WORK: (1) reproduce under full-suite dual-worktree load and capture the assertion; (2) decide
RAIL bug vs SPEC-ACCURACY bug — if the render worker genuinely cannot promise its timing under
contention, the test must pin what IS promised, not a wider margin; NEVER widen the assertion and
never add a retry; (3) fix that one; (4) if it cannot be fixed same-day once diagnosed, it.skip with
this ticket id in the title.

RAILS: the fix's own test, plus the two-direction measurement recorded in the PR (fails under load
pre-fix, passes under load post-fix, passes isolated both sides).
title: write-renderers is load-flaky under concurrent full-suite runs — diagnose and pin, never widen
